 Daily Stock Market Live
 Updated Thu, Nov 5 2026 4:18 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow drops 1,800 points; Nasdaq tumbles into correction territory on AI tech wreck: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Davis Giangiulio Hugh Leask Lee Ying Shan Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., Sept. 16, 2026. Jeenah Moon | Reuters Stocks plummeted on Thursday, erasing the sharp gains from the rally seen in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections , as investors accelerated their move away from technology stocks on fears of a data-center buildout slowdown.
 The Nasdaq Composite declined 5.52% to close at 24,315.00. The tech-heavy index slid into correction territory, falling more than 10% below a record set last month. The S&P 500 dropped 4.36% to end at 7,353.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 1,833.06 points, or 3.44%, and settled at 51,523.06. 
 The Dow more than wiped out its advance from Wednesday's massive postelection rally. All three major averages posted their worst day since April 2025.
 The small-cap Russell 2000 index decreased 4.45% and also entered a correction. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Nasdaq Composite, 5-day Stocks related to the artificial intelligence trade, particularly those linked to the chips industry and data centers, slid for a second day. Investors fear that a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress as well as victories in key gubernatorial races could decelerate the data center buildout .
 For instance, Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont — who caucuses with Democrats — has called for a national data center moratorium. In a post on X Wednesday evening, Sanders wrote that "Americans don't want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity's future."
 Chipmakers Broadcom and Nvidia respectively fell 10% and 9% Thursday, while software stock Oracle moved lower by almost 7%. Another chip stock, Qualcomm , reported earnings that beat estimates , but the stock dropped 9% on a weaker-than-expected earnings outlook. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was down more than 12% for its worst day since the Covid-19 breakout of March 2020.
 Shares of neocloud companies also retreated, with CoreWeave losing almost 10%. Nebius and Iren slid about 15% and almost 17%, amid worries about a backlash to the industry in light of the election results in various states.
 Investors are "stepping away until they get a better sense of the implications of the midterms around the AI capex cycle in particular, which is the biggest economic tailwind we've had going for us for the last, call it, three years," said Tim Holland, chief investment officer at Orion. "It's about tone and tenor from the party that did really well, incredibly well, at the federal level and at the state level."
 Thursday's selling pressure was so intense that it spread to other parts of the market. Shares of industrial giant Caterpillar declined 6%, while financial stock JPMorgan fell 4%. Aerospace name Boeing and athletic apparel giant Nike pulled back 2%.
 "Unlike yesterday, you're just seeing that the sell-off in tech, the size of it, is now feeding itself into the broader market," said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Wealth. "The rubber band is becoming increasingly stretched."
 On Wednesday, the Dow jumped more than 1,500 points to notch its best day since April 2025 after a decisive midterm win for Democrats. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite also popped more than 1% each. Areas related to AI were under pressure, however, while economically-sensitive stocks rose.
 2 Hours Ago Stocks plummet on Thursday
 The Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images U.S. equities sold off significantly during Thursday's session.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,833.06 points, or 3.44%, to settle at 51,523.06. The S&P 500 shed 4.36% to 7,353.73, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 5.52% to 24,315.00.
 — Sean Conlon 
 3 Hours Ago Mag7 was losing close to $900 billion in aggregate market value heading into final hour 
 Magnificent 7 tech stocks on display at the Nasdaq. Adam Jeffery | CNBC The Mag7 stocks were losing close to an aggregate $900 billion heading into the final hour of trading Thursday.
 Nvidia alone was worth some $374 billion less than at Wednesday's close; Tesla was down $161 billion; and Microsoft $117 billion. Apple shed nearly $59 billion in market value, Meta Platforms almost $58 billion, Amazon was lower by about $55 billion and Alphabet by more than $42 billion.
 — Scott Schnipper and Nick Wells 
 3 Hours Ago Loop downgrades Dollar Tree, says buy Ollie’s instead
 Loop Capital downgraded Dollar Tree to Hold from Buy on Thursday, maintaining its $140 price target after shares rallied more than 20% since early October. 
 “We believe our bullish fundamental outlook on Dollar Tree is largely priced in at current levels,” Loop Capital’s analyst Anthony Chukumba said. The downgrade reflects valuation concerns rather than weakening fundamentals. 
 Chukumba said Ollie's Bargain Outlet ("Ollie's") provides a more compelling long opportunity for investors seeking exposure to the deep discount retailing space heading into the fast-approaching holiday selling season.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Dollar Tree and Ollie's price chart The analyst said high gas prices and tighter household budgets will push more shoppers toward Dollar Tree ahead of the holidays. The retailer’s growing range of products at different prices also continues to lift sales at existing stores.
 “All that said,” Chukumba said, “with Dollar Tree stock trading above its historical average next fiscal year P/E multiple, we believe upside potential and downside risk are fairly balanced at current levels.”
 — Deena Zaidi 
 3 Hours Ago Truist Securities downgrades Nike Thursday
 Nike stock caught a downgrade from Truist Securities Thursday.
 The firm re-rated the sportswear retailer lower to hold from sell while keeping its $29 price target. 
 Analyst Joseph Civello said the stock's gain over the past month is due to "positive sector rotations rather than an improvement in underlying fundamentals." Over that period, shares have risen 16%.
 The rise has resulted in a stretched stock valuation that "prices in an overly optimistic turnaround," the analyst wrote. 
 Analysts also called out pressures across Nike's portfolio including weak product launches and a deteriorating outlook in its key China market.
 Truist lowered its full year 2028 earnings per share estimate to $1.30, below the Wall Street consensus of  $1.50 and the firm's prior estimate of $1.40, the firm said.
 Nike shares are down 38% year-to-date, however.
 — Paulina Likos 
 4 Hours Ago Wall Street is positive on Arm Holdings
 Rene Haas, CEO of chip tech provider Arm Holdings, holds a replica of a chip with his company's logo on it on March 5, 2025. Hasnoor Hussain | Reuters Several investment banks are positive on chip designer Arm Holdings on Thursday after the company reported strong licensing and weak royalties in its latest beat-and-raise quarter.
 "Licensing is a leading indicator of future Royalties (12-24 months) [and] suggests continued strong customer interest in custom silicon solutions," Vivek Arya at Bank of America said in a Thursday note.
 He cautioned that "Arm's increasing dependence on SoftBank for Licensing revenue could pose circular financing concerns."
 — Tobias Burns 
 4 Hours Ago Things have to get a lot worse before NYSE circuit breakers kick in
 As bad as Thursday's stock market washout is, conditions have to get a lot worse before the New York Stock Exchange circuit breakers would kick in and pause trading. At the Thursday low, the S&P bottomed out with a loss of 4.23% before recovering somewhat. 
 Level 1 and Level 2 Market-Wide Circuit Breakers that halt trading for a minimum of 15 minutes only come into effect between 9:30 am ET and 3:25 pm ET if the S&P 500 drops by 7% or more (Level 1) and 13% (Level 2). 
 A Level 3 decline of 20% or more can come into effect at any time and halts trading for the rest of the day. 
 When were the circuit breakers last used? Four times in March 2020 , twice before the major Covid lockdowns began to be put in to place on March 15, and twice after. The only other time that the circuit breakers, first introduced in the aftermath of the 1987 stock market crash, were used was once in October, 1997 during the Asian financial crisis.
 — Scott Schnipper 
 4 Hours Ago Wells Fargo raises outlook for McDonald’s
 People enter a McDonald's restaurant in Times Square, Manhattan, on Sept. 29, 2026, in New York City. KHemaz | GVN | Getty Images McDonald's jumped more than 6% on Wednesday after reporting better-than-expected earnings . Wells Fargo liked the numbers too.
 The bank reiterated its overweight rating on the fast food company's stock in a Wednesday note, and raised its price target to $300. That indicates a 7% gain from Wednesday's close. Analyst Zachary Fadem said the company's financial report showed numbers that were encouraging.
 "Q3 cleared a low bar, shares were washed out & MCD cited notable progress on value w/ new steps in '27," he wrote in the note. "Skepticism likely persists… but [Wednesday's] print is a step in the right direction."
 In afternoon trading Thursday, shares were pulling back by more than 1%. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon McDonald's 5-day. — Davis Giangiulio  
 4 Hours Ago Tech sell-off drags Nasdaq Composite below its 200-day moving average
 Market information at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite tumbled more than 5% on Thursday afternoon, sending the index below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Nasdaq Composite in the past day The S&P 500 is also near its 200-day moving average, trading less than 1% from that level. If the broad market index were to slip below that threshold, that would mark its first time doing so since April.
 Big tech players dipping below their respective 200-day moving averages include Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Marvell Technology, Micron Technology, Sandisk and Cisco.
 The sell-off in the tech sector comes as a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections is now raising fears that the data center build-out could be in for a slowdown.
 When an asset or an index trades below its 200-day moving average, it suggests that a longer-term downtrend may be unfolding. This is especially the case if it closes below the 200-day moving average.
 — Darla Mercado and Nick Wells 
 5 Hours Ago All S&P 500 sectors suffer losses
 All 11 S&P 500 sectors were trading in negative territory on Thursday afternoon as selling across the U.S. equity market picked up steam.
 Information technology was the biggest laggard, dropping 6.6%. The group's declines were then followed by a fall in consumer discretionary stocks as well as industrials. Those two sectors were down 4.1% and 4%, respectively.
 Most stocks in the broad market index were also trading lower, as the S&P 500 recorded 419 losers and 84 gainers. The index was last down 3.9%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 5 Hours Ago Wall Street’s fear gauge jumps to highest level since March
 The Cboe Volatility Index briefly climbed to 28.09 Thursday, its highest level since March 31, when it touched 29.64. Currently, the VIX is at 26.26.
 The VIX, which measures expected stock-market volatility and is often called Wall Street's "fear gauge," last traded above 30 on March 30, when it reached 31.52.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon VIX — Deena Zaidi and Gina Francolla 
 6 Hours Ago Chip stocks plunge for worst day since March 2020
 Traders work at the New York Stock Exchange on Nov. 2, 2026. NYSE Chip stocks tumbled Thursday, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF falling close to 11%. A closing decline greater than 10.44% marks its worst day since March 2020 with every component down more than 6%.
 After a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress , which could spell more regulation of the AI buildout, stocks tied to the AI trade, particularly those linked to the chips industry and data centers slid for a second day. 
 Astera Labs and MACOM Technology Solutions fell roughly 17% and 18%, respectively. AMD and Micron dropped 15% each, while Arm slid about 12%. The SOXX was down 15% for the week.
 — Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells 
 6 Hours Ago Stock market wipeout is lessening pressure on the Fed to hike rates in December
 The equity market sell-off is easing pressure on the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates at its last meeting of the year, on Dec. 9.
 Odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates a quarter percentage point from their current 3.75%-4.00% range have fallen to 70.1%, down from 82.7% on Wednesday and 79.9% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool , which is based on 30-day fed funds futures prices. 
 Conversely, the chance that the Kevin Warsh-led central bank will be able to keep rates where they are in December stands at 29.9% at midday Thursday, up from 17.3% on Wednesday and 20.1% a week ago
 — Scott Schnipper 
 6 Hours Ago Global Payments trades higher despite lack of an immediate buyout
 Piotr Swat | Sopa Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Global Payments didn't use its third-quarter earnings report to confirm speculation that the company is working out a deal to go private , but it did show that it is continuing to integrate its Worldpay acquisition, which CNBC expects will support its stock in the future . 
 Shares are trading higher despite the broader market pullback. The payments company earned $3.58 per share after adjustments, in line with the FactSet consensus estimate and an increase of 10% year-on-year. It reaffirmed its full year 2026 outlook.
 Adjusted operating margin rose 220 basis points to 42.5%, powered by the successful capture of operational efficiencies and synergies from the Worldpay integration. The company now expects Worldpay synergies of $650 million, up from $600 million previously, by the end of 2028. 
 Global Payments all-in-one Genius point-of-sale and business management platform saw strong growth in the quarter with bookings more than doubling year-on-year. Performance in the Middle East continues to be hurt by the war, but was "generally in line with our expectations," CFO Josh Whipple said on the earnings call. He categorized the recovery as "very uneven and inconsistent." 
 Management declined to comment on reported buyout talks with Clayton Dubilier & Rice and shareholder GTCR, saying it doesn't "comment on market rumors or speculation."
 On the call, CEO Cameron Bready said he is "not really going to be able to get into the reporting or any of the specifics around it." 
 — Justin Zacks 
 7 Hours Ago AI declines are just getting started, Macro Research Board warns
 Declines for the super intelligence, or artificial intelligence, trade still have a long way to go, investment strategists at the Macro Research Board are warning on Thursday.
 "The shakeout in A.I.-related stocks has much further to run," the firm said in a Thursday note. Researchers said that "investors are beginning to question excessive forward profit estimates."
 They recommend diversifying away from tech stocks amid general sensitivities in equities. 
 "In this environment, our bet has been a churn in the aggregate U.S. and global stocks indexes (at least for now), but with a meaningful rotation underneath the surface (including divergences in the absolute price of stocks/sectors)," they said, adding that monetary and fiscal policy are not currently restrictive.
 — Tobias Burns 
 7 Hours Ago Tech stocks are selling off hard, entering vicious correction
 The Micron Technology offices in San Jose, California, Dec. 16, 2025. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Tech stocks are getting pummeled on Thursday.
 Chip stocks central to the AI trade in particular are getting walloped. Micron and AMD are down 16% and GPU powerhouse Nvidia is down 8%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon MU, 1-day — Tobias Burns 
 7 Hours Ago Analysts are meh on Qualcomm after weak earnings forecast
 Thomas Fuller | Lightrocket | Getty Images Wall Street is measured on the outlook for Qualcomm after the company delivered a weak earnings forecast on Wednesday. Analyst Stacey Rasgon at Bernstein has a market-perform rating on the stock and a price target of $155; Joseph Moore at Morgan Stanley has an equal-weight rating and a price target of $197.
 Customer diversification is the buzzword on the Street for Qualcomm, as mentioned in multiple research notes.
 "The debate has shifted to diversification: ambitious data center targets of $5B in FY27 and $15B+ in FY29, and continued strength in autos," Morgan Stanley's Moore said on Thursday.
 — Tobias Burns 
 8 Hours Ago Gold and silver extend post-election rally, head for best week since August
 Gold and silver bars of various sizes at the precious metals dealer Pro Aurum in Munich. Sven Hoppe | Picture Alliance | Getty Images Gold and silver futures climbed Thursday as a weaker U.S. dollar and lower Treasury yields supported a rally following the U.S. midterm elections. Falling oil prices eased inflation concerns.
 December gold futures touched $4,155.80 an ounce, their highest since October 22, while December silver reached $53.49, its highest since October 29.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Gold stock price The yellow metal is up more than 5% this week as silver has gained more than 6%. Gold was on pace for its strongest weekly advance since the week ended Aug. 7, while silver was heading for its best week since Aug. 21.
 Gold miners joined the rally, with the VanEck Gold Miners ETF up about 1% on Thursday and more than 10% this week. Harmony Gold and IAMGOLD are among the leaders, each gaining more than 13% this week. Equinox Gold has risen more than 15% on the week.
 — Deena Zaidi and Gina Francolla 
 8 Hours Ago Nasdaq dips into correction territory
 The Nasdaq Composite tumbled into correction territory on Thursday, trading 10% below a record close set last month. The benchmark was down 3.9% on the day as chipmakers sold off. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Nasdaq Composite dips into correction — Fred Imbert 
 8 Hours Ago VIX moves above 22
 The CBOE Volatility Index rose on Thursday as equity sell-off picked up steam, with Wall Street's so-called fear gauge last up 22.59.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon .VIX, 1-day — Sean Conlon 
 9 Hours Ago Dow opens higher
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average began Thursday's session in the green.
 The blue-chip Dow added 334 points, or 0.6%, just after the opening bell. The S&P 500 dipped 0.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 0.7%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 9 Hours Ago Jobless claims drop again as layoffs near lowest since 1969
 Jobseekers wait to speak with recruiters during the Catalyst Career Group Dallas Job Fair in Dallas, Texas, US, on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. Dylan Hollingsworth | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jobless claims slipped further last week, hovering around levels not seen since the late 1960s, the Labor Department reported Thursday.
 Initial filings for unemployment claims totaled a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ended Oct. 31, down 6,000 from the prior period and below the Dow Jones consensus estimate for 197,000. The total tied for the lowest since July, which was the bottom going back to September 1969.
 Continuing claims, which run a week behind, rose 23,000 to 1.72 million.
 — Jeff Cox 
 10 Hours Ago Productivity spikes, labor costs slide
 Productivity posted a stronger-than-expected jump in the third quarter while the portion of output that showed up in worker pay hit a record low, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Thursday.
 Nonfarm business sector productivity surged 3.6% for the period, up from 2.1% in the second quarter and well ahead of the Dow Jones consensus estimate for 2.9%. Compensation less productivity, a metric known as unit labor costs, contracted 0.7%.
 At the the same, the percentage of output that goes to workers in the form of compensation, known as the labor share, slipped further to 53%, the lowest in a data series that dates back to 1947.
 — Jeff Cox 
 10 Hours Ago Shake Shack, Peloton and Wendy's among the stocks making the biggest moves premarket
 Check out the companies making headlines before the bell: 
 Shake Shack — Shares rose 3.8% after the fast-food chain published its third-quarter results. Adjusted earnings per share of 40 cents topped an LSEG estimate of 35 cents per share. Revenue of $423 million was just below the $426 million consensus. Management also reaffirmed the company's full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $1.6 billion to $1.7 billion.
 Peloton Interactive — The maker of fitness equipment jumped 7% after Peloton Interactive posted fiscal first-quarter revenue of $559 million, besting the LSEG consensus estimate of $554 million. However, earnings of 19 cents per share missed the 21 cents expected.
 Wendy's — Shares were little changed after the fast food chain rejected a $1.4 billion takeover offer from a Trian Fund Management-led group. The group late last month offered $7.35 per share in cash to take Wendy's private.
 Read the full list here . 
 — Sarah Min 
 11 Hours Ago Why Trump's reaction to Democratic victory in the midterms aided Wednesday’s rally
 US President Donald Trump speaks at the White House ballroom construction site in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. Annabelle Gordon | Bloomberg | Getty Images The stock market skyrocketed on Wednesday on the heels of a decisive sweep for Democrats in the 2026 midterm elections . But that was not necessarily the only driver of the climb.
 "President Trump's acknowledgement of the Democrats' victory in the midterms and his expressed openness to collaborating with the opposition have helped markets to rally on hopes that contestation of the results and more adverse polarization can be avoided," said Thomas Hempell, Generali Investments senior economist. 
 Trump told The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal overnight Tuesday that he accepted the results and would work with Democrats. Those headlines coincided with a rebound in stock market futures.
 Read the full story here .
 — Sean Conlon 
 11 Hours Ago Wendy's rejects Trian takeover bid
 Wendy's shares were down slightly after the fast food chain on Thursday rejected a a $1.4 billion takeover offer from a Trian Fund Management-led group.
 The group late last month offered $7.35 per share in cash to take Wendy's private. 
 — Fred Imbert 
 13 Hours Ago The midterms could fuel the K-shaped AI trade
 The U.S. midterms could widen the AI divide: tighter data center rules may reward tech giants with capacity in hand and squeeze debt-funded companies trying to catch up.
 Democratic victories in key gubernatorial races raised the prospect of tougher scrutiny for data center projects, adding to investor concerns about how quickly new capacity can be built and financed.
 How the midterms could fuel the K-shaped AI trade 13 Hours Ago OpenAI pledges to pay for data center power after election highlights AI concerns
 Sam Altman, chief executive officer and co-founder of OpenAI Inc., speaks during a Bloomberg Television interview at OpenAI DevDay in San Francisco, California, US, on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. Minh Connors | Bloomberg | Getty Images OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI.
 OpenAI pledges to halt NDAs in new data center policy proposal after election rebuke 14 Hours Ago U.K.'s FTSE 100 hits three-month high
 The FTSE 100 touched a three-month high on Thursday morning.
 The U.K.'s blue-chip index rose as much as 119 points to 10,948, up more than 1.1% in early trading and reaching its highest level since Aug 7. The index was last seen 0.86% higher.
 The rise comes as traders await the Bank of England's latest interest rate decision, due later Thursday. The market expects the central bank's rate-setting Monetary Policy Committee to raise rates by 25 basis points to 4% from 3.75% — its first hike in more than three years.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon FTSE 100. Shares in British lenders moved higher ahead of the BoE's decision, due at 12:00 p.m. in London (7:00 a.m. E.T.). Barclays was up 2.2%, while Lloyds Banking Group added 1.9% and NatWest was 1.4% higher.
 Sterling was up almost 0.1% against the dollar at $1.3482.
 — Hugh Leask 
 15 Hours Ago Rheinmetall shares plunge 16% after outlook cut as military contracts stall
 German Rheinmetall MAN tactical military transport vehicles parked in the Edvard Peperko military barracks. Luka Dakskobler | Lightrocket | Getty Images German defense giant Rheinmetall cut its full-year guidance late Wednesday, citing delays to military contracts and ammunition deliveries, sending shares down as much as 16% in early trading.
 It marks the company's second outlook cut since August, when Germany scrapped plans to build warships in what would have been Rheinmetall's biggest order since World War II. 
The defense company now expects sales to rise to around 13.2 billion euros ($14.9 billion) in 2026, down from a prior outlook range of between 13.7 billion and 14.2 billion euros. It is expected to have an operating margin of around 18.5%, down from the previously expected 19%.
 Rheinmetall said it's revising its 2026 guidance due to delays in the German military's Arminius Boxer project, now expected to be commissioned next year, and setbacks in artillery ammunition acceptance testing. 
 Read more here .
 — Elsa Ohlen 
 15 Hours Ago European stock markets open in the green
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 was up 0.48% shortly after 8:05 a.m. in London (3:05 a.m. in E.T.), as the continent's major bourses and sectors opened the day in the green.
 Basic resources led gains, rising 2.51%, followed by autos and parts, which rose 2.05%. Travel and leisure stocks added 1.76%. Oil and gas reversed by 1.84%.
 In Paris, France's CAC 40 was up 1.08%, as the U.K. FTSE 100 advanced 1.05% in London. In Milan, the Italian FTSE MIB was up almost 0.1%, and Germany's DAX added 0.16% in Frankfurt.
 — Hugh Leask 
 16 Hours Ago World's biggest spirit maker says Iran war is leading to continued volatility 
 A customers grabs a bottle of Johnnie Walker Black Label whisky, a Diageo Plc product, for sale at a liquor store in Johannesburg, South Africa, on Thursday, July 31, 2025. The Kenya-based unit of Diageo Plc reported profit for the year through end June of 12.2 billion shillings ($94.4 million) Photographer: Leon Sadiki/Bloomberg via Getty Images Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Diageo said the U.S-Iran war is continuing to weigh on operations in its first-quarter trading update on Thursday after net sales rose marginally. 
 The British spirits giant, which owns brands including Johnnie Walker scotch whisky, Guinness stout, Smirnoff vodka and Tanqueray gin, said net sales were up 1.2% to $4.9 billion year-on-year, while organic volume growth declined 0.1% and price/mix was up 0.7%. 
 "Whilst the market remains challenging, and volatility continues given the geopolitical uncertainty and impact of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East on energy, supply and distribution, results in the first quarter represent a small step in the right direction," Diageo's CEO Sir Dave Lewis said in the update. 
 Diageo said earlier this year that it's embarking on a restructuring strategy which will amount to $1.2 billion in savings over 2027 and 2028. 
 — Sawdah Bhaimiya 
 16 Hours Ago South Korea’s Kospi plunges 5% as Asia-Pacific markets close mixed
 Asia-Pacific markets closed mixed Thursday.
 South Korea's Kospi fell 5.28%, leading losses in the region to end the trading day at 5,383.8. The small-cap, tech-focused Kosdaq fell 5.11%, closing at 678.41.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 dropped 1.79% to 61,077.9, and the broad-based Topix gained 1.16% at 3,940.39.
 Mainland China's CSI 300 rose 0.29% to 4,113.41, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was up 3.61% as of its last hour of trade.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 added 2.61% to 9,065.1.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 16 Hours Ago Maersk lifts profit outlook for third time as higher freight rates boost earnings
 The container ship Gunde Maersk docked at the Port of Oakland on June 24, 2024, in Oakland, California. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Maersk generated $4.7 billion in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the third-quarter, up from $2.6 billion in the same period last year.
 In its third-quarter interim report, the Danish shipping and logistics mainstay raised its full-year profit guidance for a third time this year to between $14 billion and $14.5 billion, up from $10.5-12.5 billion.
 Maersk said the Strait of Hormuz closure, adverse weather conditions in East Asia and broader congestion helped push average freight rates 46% higher, driving strong performance within its Ocean business.
 "Despite continued geopolitical uncertainty and disruptions, global trade has remained remarkably resilient," Vincent Clerc, Maersk CEO, said.
 "Demand is being driven not only by consumer spending, but increasingly by major investments in electrification, energy and the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, generating significant flows of industrial cargo around the world."
   — Hugh Leask 
 16 Hours Ago European stock markets set to start Thursday's session higher
 The U.K. FTSE 100 is set to open 1.11% higher, with stock markets across Europe expected to begin Thursday's session in positive territory.
 Futures tied to the Stoxx 50 were up 0.32% ahead of the opening bell. 
 France's CAC 40 is seen 0.29% higher, with Germany's DAX rising 0.36% and the Italian FTSE MIB up almost 0.1%
 — Hugh Leask 
 17 Hours Ago Commerzbank’s net profit soars 45% in the third quarter
 The logo of German bank Commerzbank seen on a branch office near the Commerzbank Tower in Frankfurt. Daniel Roland | Afp | Getty Images Commerzbank 's net profit reached 859 million euros ($967 million) in the third quarter, a 45% year-on-year jump, as third-quarter revenues rose 9% to 3.2 billion euros.
 The rise was driven by a rise in securities-related fees, along with higher interest income from corporate lending and deposits.
 Operating profits rose 17% to 40 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with net profits up 41% to 2.7 billion, which the German lender described in its quarterly earnings update Thursday as its best nine-month result on record.
 Meanwhile, net interest income increased to 2.1 billion in the third quarter, as common equity tier (CET) 1 ratio — a measure of a bank's solvency — was 14.2% for the period, down slightly from the previous second quarter's 14.4%.
 With Italian bank UniCredit on track to acquire the Frankfurt-listed lender, Commerzbank said it expects the remaining regulatory approvals for the deal to be approved in the fourth quarter or by early 2027.
 "We are convinced that together with UniCredit, we can create value by consistently leveraging the strengths of both banks," said Commerzbank CEO Bettina Orlopp.
 — Hugh Leask 
 18 Hours Ago Indonesia third-quarter growth beats expectations at 5.47%
 Indonesia's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, expanding 5.47% from a year earlier.
 That surpassed the 5.18% expansion expected by economists polled by Reuters, and was faster than the 5.29% seen in the preceding quarter. 
 Growth was powered by government spending, as well as accommodation and food service activities. 
 The data comes at a time when the country is seeing widespread student protests over income disparity, cost of living and environmental concerns.
 The country's benchmark index rose nearly 2%.
